title: Warming Up a New Sending Domain: The Boring Playbook That Works
author: Juan Rodriguez
excerpt: New domains start with zero trust. The week-by-week warmup discipline that gets you to the inbox without shortcuts.
content:
Inbox providers treat a new sending domain like a stranger at the door: polite suspicion until proven otherwise. Warming up is how you prove otherwise - slowly, consistently, without hacks.

Authenticate before you send anything

SPF, DKIM and DMARC in place from message one. Sending warm-up mail without authentication is introducing yourself while wearing a mask. Alignment between the visible From domain and the authentication domains matters most.

Start with the people who want you

Your first sends go to your most engaged subscribers - recent openers, recent buyers, people who asked to hear from you this week. Opens and replies are the votes that build reputation; a warm-up list of disengaged contacts votes against you.

Grow volume on a schedule

Small consistent daily sends, increasing gradually over four to eight weeks. The pattern inbox providers reward is predictability: same sender, steady growth, low complaints. A spike from zero to fifty thousand on day three is how domains get a reputation that takes months to repair.

Watch the right signals

Bounce rate, complaint rate, and provider-specific deferrals in your logs. If Gmail starts temp-failing you, slow down - the machine is telling you the pace is wrong. Warm-up is one of the few places in email where patience is the entire strategy.
